What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(4,-4)$ and passes through the point $(7,5).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(4,-4)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-4)^{2}=4p(y+4).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(7,5),$ we substitute $x=7$ and $y=5$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(7-4)^{2} & =4p(5+4) \\ 9 & =4p(9) \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =y+4.\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-4)^{2} & =y+4 \\ 16 & =y+4 \\ y & =16-4 \\ y & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $12.$
